chunks: And among what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, that 'Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about the salat in the two Eids.

So he said: The salat in both of them is the same. The Imam says the opening takbir of the salat completely, as he does in the obligatory prayer, then he adds in the first rak'ah three takbirs and in the second three, apart from the takbir of the salat, and the ruku' and the sujud. And if he wishes, three and five; and if he wishes, five and seven, after attaching that to the odd number.

Thus, the way to understand these two narrations is taqiyyah, because they accord with the doctrines of many among the 'ammah, and we do not act upon it; and the consensus of the rightly guided sect is upon what we have stated earlier.

key_terms.إِجْمَاعُ: consensus, here referring to the agreement of the Imami community
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in expression under certain circumstances
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid prayers, namely Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer used here as the point of comparison
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the odd-numbered pattern to which the takbir count is aligned
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: additional pronouncements of Allahu akbar within the prayer

ai.seo_question: How many takbirs are there in the Eid prayer according to this narration in al-Istibsar, and how is it interpreted?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the number of takbirs in the salat of the two Eids and reports a narration describing one manner of performing them. It then states that these narrations are to be understood as issued in taqiyyah because they conform to positions held by many among the 'ammah, and that the authoritative practice is based on what had been presented earlier.
